screenshots.exception_caveat: Held and disconnected UI state screenshots do not establish a matched current delivery fence.
screenshots.dimension_caveat: Full-page captures, not identical viewport crops. Desktop PNGs are 1800x1125, disconnected is 488x1055, narrow Book/held are 469x1056, narrow before is 469x2299, and empty search is 469x1533. The original operator reports fullPage=true and explains width 469 as a 375 CSS-pixel content area after a 15 CSS-pixel scrollbar at DPR 1.25; disconnected captures the full 390 CSS-pixel width. Before narrow document height was 1839 CSS pixels with the old stacked Book starting at 1058.94 CSS pixels. Preserve reported viewport separately from actual PNG dimensions; do not claim pixel-matched narrow views.
screenshots.narrow_comparison_caveat: after-recorded-narrow-390-book.png intentionally selects the Book pane; it is not the same view as before-recorded-narrow-390.png.
screenshots.paper_receipt_caveat: Do not include /tmp/lob-after-paper.png as visual receipt proof: it shows only the narrow form. Parent-reported actual native IOC text result is scenario metadata in summary.json, explicitly fake 1000 USDT funds, 10bps, date 2026-11-01; not a receipt screenshot.

reproduction.working_directory: Repository root; retained scripts resolve repository paths from their own locations. These scripts/configurations are permanent documented reproducers.
prerequisites: Existing repository .venv with native runtime dependencies.
Existing frontend/node_modules containing the repository-pinned @playwright/test and its already-installed Chromium shell.
Current frontend/dist build; before comparison additionally requires the separately saved build matching before-assets.json. Build bytes are not included in this archive.
Use unused loopback ports; existing browser output JSON paths are deliberately refused.

Baseline git object 49f2d0a4bb07a4d0816c0644890756d740b3cc7d for core-before/crossover; tests/test_workstation_paper.py fixture for paper-workload; native reference capture at the recorded relative path for replay-workload.
reproduction.execution_notes: Run servers in separate terminals, browser workloads sequentially, and interrupt servers afterward. Replace the before --dist path with the location of the hash-matching saved build when moving machines. For narrow measurements use --width 390 on both runs and distinct output paths; accepted durations remain 20 or 30 seconds.
reproduction.workload_scope: The browser reproducer is synthetic-demo-only and refuses a non-demo API-preferred source. Its optional screenshot is paused delivery 2000 at DPR 1 and height 900, not a reproduction of the separately captured recorded screenshots at delivery 2057/DPR 1.25. Optional --capture exposes a local read-only recorded source in the native server but does not change the browser workload.
reproduction.safety: Loopback only; native backend has enable_live=False and registry=None. No wallet, collector, live orders, custom browser, downloads, routing, fixtures, or injected data.
reproduction.playwright_notes: Use an already-running native server with final frontend at default http://127.0.0.1:8015/; optional LOB_E2E_BASE_URL accepts only a loopback HTTP origin. Configuration uses existing frontend node_modules/Chromium; no auto-start, download, build or bypass. Unique temporary output directory avoids root test-results. Parent owns execution and result reporting.
reproduction.native_notes: core-before.py requires baseline revision in local git and checks its original-book SHA256 before in-memory execution; no checkout mutation. Pass the desired benchmark arguments unchanged. Final reports used 20000 initial levels/side and 300 deltas (100/s normal, 200/s burst). crossover.py alternates 24 before/after applications per 17 depth/touch cases. Crossover, paper and replay emit JSON to stdout; choose fresh destinations rather than replacing archived evidence. Repeat independent runs a,b,c for three-run aggregation. Historical paper results are archived observations, not reproduced by loading only the historical book module.
